feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target title. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, tighter section consolidation, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at one organization support trust and show increasing responsibility.  
- Strong strategic/technical blend: combines communications leadership with Drupal, analytics, workflow, and multimedia capability.  
- Good use of scale indicators: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools add substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more results, not just responsibilities: include measurable outcomes such as traffic growth, engagement lifts, email performance, cost savings, process efficiency, or campaign impact.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; choose one style for serial commas (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” instead. No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it and adding one clearer differentiator will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with your strongest current value: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with a tighter, more senior framing.
- Consider this rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Specializes in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and scalable editorial workflows that improve coordination, governance, and audience engagement. Brings deep experience in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” are repeated in Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” and “stakeholder coordination” also appear elsewhere; keep the intro high-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, senior-level terms: “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”; “Web & CMS administration” → “Web platform governance & CMS management.”
- Prioritize strategic and recent strengths first: digital strategy, platform modernization, editorial systems, analytics, and advocacy/public-sector communications.
- Reduce repetition between “workflow design” and “workflow & systems architecture” by combining them into one clearer competency.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & platform modernization • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform governance & CMS management • Editorial systems, workflow design & content operations • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Stakeholder and cross-functional coordination • Public-sector, policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Overlaps significantly with the header summary and Topline Skills; consider trimming this section or using it only for broad themes not listed elsewhere.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also repeats Soft Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a services list rather than a results-oriented experience entry. Tighten the phrasing and foreground 2–3 highest-impact contributions, especially AI search, Drupal campaign builds, and communications systems.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary line: “Embedded as a full-time consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and communications operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership verbs: “Led,” “Built,” “Designed,” “Implemented,” “Established.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-focused bullets; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics + governance/usability into one operations bullet.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, publishing speed, stakeholder teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with NACo bullets on governance, analytics infrastructure, and Drupal/web modernization; emphasize new consulting scope and AI-enabled search to differentiate.
- “Microsite structures” and campaign examples already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/operational scope, and distinguish strategic leadership from execution covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable business impact where possible: email engagement growth, social growth, production volume, reporting adoption, time saved, reduced vendor spend, or faster publishing cycles.
- Tighten phrasing: replace “including”/“along with” constructions with action + result; keep 4–5 bullets max and lead each with a strong verb.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role’s newsletter/social/video operations; focus this entry on enterprise leadership, modernization, analytics, and governance.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with older multimedia bullets unless framed as a new organizational capability or cost/capacity gain.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item reads generic and overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what changed or scaled under your leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to stress ownership and scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets around concrete outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-led: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems bullet: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows by coordinating communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency across digital channels.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” closely repeats the Director role; keep this item more tactical.
- Weekly video/livestream language overlaps with the 2015–2018 role, so frame this as scaling/formalizing the program rather than starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent experience. It should be tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership strengths rather than repeating broad digital/communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, higher-signal wording tied to recent work:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Content governance & editorial operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy communications
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel” to “Cross-channel” for a more modern, concise tone.
- “Editorial systems and governance” is strong; “content governance & editorial operations” reads more active and leadership-oriented.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable outcomes for experience bullets rather than skills lines.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “governance” already appear in the header/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact same phrasing across sections.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies—use one version consistently.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills area, make it more selective, grouped, and tied to the most recent/high-impact work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped capabilities, not a long tool list: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Prioritize recent strengths proven in current/NACo roles: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations, and workflow automation.
- Remove lower-priority platforms unless they are target-role requirements; consider dropping WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages from this topline item.
- If space allows, sharpen phrasing to outcomes-oriented language: “Enterprise CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search and discovery” sound stronger than generic platform names.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost exactly; keep topline skills higher-level and leave full platform/tool inventory below.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies; avoid repeating identical wording.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool dump and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics capability and decision-making impact, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting and optimization” rather than a pure software list.
- Tighten to 5–7 items and group related tools: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio & Power BI” instead of listing each separately.
- Add higher-value phrasing tied to seniority: “KPI framework design,” “executive/leadership dashboards,” “behavior and performance analysis,” “measurement for web modernization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “- Analytics strategy and measurement planning - KPI framework design - Executive dashboards and leadership reporting - GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio & Power BI - User behavior analysis (Microsoft Clarity) - SEO, content and performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT almost exactly.
- “Leadership reporting” also overlaps with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery scope, technical depth, and production leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio Operations & Live Event Delivery**
- Tighten and sharpen the list: **Broadcast-style video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event production workflows**
- If you want more impact, add one outcome-oriented qualifier: **Built and operated in-house studio capabilities for advocacy programming and live events**
- Keep terms aligned with recent experience; “broadcast-quality,” “in-house studio,” and “hybrid event delivery” better reflect the 2022–2024 leadership role than generic “editing”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates Core Competencies: **“Multimedia production and livestream operations.”** Consider removing one or making this version more technical.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” and “Livestreaming” are close; combine to avoid repetition.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. Use this space to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, while trimming lower-value items.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add light qualifiers to show level, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, governance)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint/Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, split by strength: **Primary: Drupal, WordPress | Working knowledge: SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Consider replacing GitHub Pages with a more business-relevant platform only if you’ve used one materially; otherwise keep it but de-emphasize it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly repeats “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; differentiate this section by showing proficiency level rather than repeating names only.
- Drupal already appears heavily in recent experience, so avoid overloading this item with extra Drupal wording unless it adds specificity.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” It should emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for specificity and consistency: “Front-end development: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group by function to improve scanability: “Implementation & integration: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add scope/outcome language in parentheses, e.g., “Google Tag Manager (tag deployment and event tracking)” or “GitHub Actions (deployment/workflow automation)”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Front-end development (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • Technical integrations (APIs, Google Tag Manager) • Lightweight serverless and deployment workflows (Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions)”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” in Topline Skills; keep detail here and shorten the topline version.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may overlap with GitHub Actions; avoid repeating both unless differentiated.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere, so this item should be tighter and more systems-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strongest/relevant tools first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If accurate, add light functional context instead of a pure list: **Airtable systems • Power Automate and Zapier integrations • Jira/Asana/Trello project workflows • Slack and Teams collaboration**
- Consider dropping one lower-value PM tool if space is tight; too many similar platforms can dilute perceived depth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact same phrasing.
- Slack and Teams are collaboration tools, not automation systems; grouping them here is fine, but the title should reflect that.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too generic and underplays your stronger, recent email leadership in NACo roles. It should signal scale and use case, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** _(enterprise email campaigns, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, member communications)_
- If accurate, strengthen with scope: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp — platforms used for high-volume newsletters, segmented member outreach and campaign communications**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; order by recency/relevance, likely **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp** if NACo work centered there.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and multiple work-experience bullets on email/newsletters; avoid repeating outcomes here.
- If you can’t substantiate hands-on use of all three systems, trim the list rather than dilute credibility.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any measurable outputs you can add.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete contributions and outcomes where possible: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly videos, audience growth, or workflow improvements.
- Tighten the management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised day-to-day work of a digital media associate.”
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped formalize digital workflows while mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow language already used in later NACo roles unless you can specify a unique improvement.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or “firsts” so it adds value without overlapping too much with later NACo digital roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the digital work more concrete: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support organizational communications and member engagement.”
- Keep the strongest differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes, audience growth, stakeholder reach, or types of programs/policy areas supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on innovation/research support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid broad claims about digital leadership here, since stronger, more recent evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.
